items.abstract: During the Holocene, human activity increasingly influenced small mammal population dynamics and geographic distribution. Despite their relevance, studies on Middle and Late Holocene (8.2 - 2 kyr BP) small mammal assemblages remain limited, particularly in the Western Mediterranean region, where anthropogenic translocations played a key role in species dispersal. Within a research framework addressing the introduction of commensal and wild rodents, we developed a multidisciplinary approach to analyse assemblages from key Late Holocene sites: Cueva del Estrecho and Cueva de Nerja (Spain), and Rirha (Morocco). Our methodology integrates 2D Geometric Morphometrics (GMM) of murine molars with Machine Learning (ML) classification techniques to resolve taxonomic uncertainties. These analyses are complemented by ancient DNA (aDNA) and direct radiocarbon dating (14C) of rodent mandibles, providing both taxonomic validation and a robust chronological framework. We focus specifically on species of the genus Mus, particularly Mus musculus domesticus and Mus spretus, both known to have been accidentally translocated by humans during the Recent Prehistory. Their dispersal is closely linked to the expansion of maritime activity and trade networks across the Mediterranean realm (1). Accurate identification of Mus remains provides robust evidence for reconstructing the details of the introduction of M. spretus into the Iberian Peninsula from North Africa, as well as the arrival of the house mouse on both shores of the western Mediterranean basin from the Levant (2, 3). Our findings contribute understanding early biological invasions, now a major threat to global biodiversity. The house mouse represents a model for studying human-mediated dispersal processes. This study highlights the value of integrating archaeological, palaeontological, and molecular approaches to investigate the origins of anthropogenic environmental change.
items.summary: 《追踪西地中海地区小鼠物种早期人类介导的扩散》：该研究整合鼠类臼齿二维几何形态测量与机器学习分类，并结合古DNA和放射性碳定年，分析西班牙与摩洛哥晚全新世遗址中鼠属遗存，以厘清家鼠与阿尔及利亚鼠的物种鉴定及人类介导的扩散过程，值得关注生物入侵与人类活动关系的研究者阅读。
items.title: Tracing early human-mediated dispersal of mouse species in the Western Mediterranean

items.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) technologies have often been utilized for fast fabrication of structures with complex geometries. The first step for process planning and geometric evaluation is the effective segmentation of features of interest from geometric measurements (i.e., point clouds) of as-deposited parts. These features can range from local distortions introduced by process parameter fluctuations to decomposing the whole geometry into a several freeform shapes. However, manual segmentation of large point cloud data is time consuming and often inaccurate. This study proposes an unsupervised framework for automatic segmentation of geometric features caused by freeform designs or excessive material accumulation. The algorithm starts by transforming the point cloud coordinates to a space for which height corresponds to material accumulation. In this space, the quantile function of the transformed height encodes information of the amount of local regions with material accumulation. The quantile function is used to obtain thresholds for contour generation and iterative shape segmentation. A case study involving four Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) printed cylindrical components and one Stereolithography (SLA) printed dental part demonstrates the method's robustness and interpretability. The results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in the presence of complex geometries.
items.summary: 《基于分位数的增材制造零件几何特征自动分割阈值方法》：该研究提出一种无监督框架，用于自动分割增材制造点云中由自由曲面设计或材料过度堆积形成的几何特征，通过坐标变换与分位函数生成阈值进行轮廓提取和迭代形状分割，并以四个电弧增材制造圆柱件和一个光固化牙科件验证了方法的稳健性与可解释性，值得关注增材制造几何检测与自动形态分析的研究者阅读。
items.title: Quantile-Based Thresholding for Automated Segmentation of Geometric Features in Additive Manufactured Parts

items.title: Biological relatedness, funerary practices and kinship in Neolithic France: reflections on sample size

items.title: Chrono-grounding of the Micoquian and Aurignacian occupations at Piekary III open-air site (Krakow, Poland)
